name: New Ventures BC Competition
summary: A yearly competition for early technology ventures with a BC resident on the team. Prizes are cash, with no equity taken.
amount: CAD 80,000 cash first prize, CAD 45,000 second, CAD 25,000 third (in packages worth more), CAD 10,000 specialty awards; 2026 figures subject to change

deadline.note: Annual competition; the 2026 round finished in September 2026; the 2027 round is not yet announced

next_steps: Check the 2027 call on the official site when it opens
Confirm a team member is a BC resident
Keep non-grant funding raised under CAD 1 million and the company under 5 years old
Pay the CAD 200 entry fee only with Luca's approval

name: Creative Destruction Lab (CDL)
provider: Creative Destruction Lab (non-profit, Rotman School of Management origin)
summary: A non-profit program of mentoring for early science and technology ventures, with Health and AI streams. There are no fees and no equity, but the program needs your time at scheduled sessions.
amount: No fees, no equity; mentoring from investor-mentors, with no guaranteed investment

deadline.note: Applications are open for the 2026/27 program year on the official site; decisions come in early September

next_steps: Apply to the AI or Health stream on the CDL portal
Block the scheduled session days in the calendar (the FAQ gives both four and five)
Confirm the dates in the CDL application portal

name: Mitacs Accelerate Entrepreneur
summary: Funds a research intern from a Canadian university to work on a startup, with the company paying half. The startup must be incorporated and housed in an approved incubator.
amount: CAD 15,000 per 4-month internship: CAD 7,500 from Mitacs and CAD 7,500 from the company
next_steps: Incorporate a Canadian company (sole proprietorships are not eligible)
Place the startup in an approved incubator for the project
Find a Canadian university supervisor and intern
Pay the CAD 7,500 company share only with Luca's approval

name: Futurpreneur Canada startup loan
summary: A startup loan and mentoring for young Canadian founders who live in Canada and run a young business.
amount: Varies, see official page
next_steps: Check the age range (18 to 39 at application) on the official page
Confirm you are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident living in Canada
Check the loan amount for the offering you qualify for

name: NRC IRAP (Industrial Research Assistance Program)
provider: National Research Council Canada (NRC), Government of Canada
summary: Non-repayable support and advisory help for incorporated Canadian SMEs developing technology in Canada. Sole proprietorships and partnerships are not eligible.
amount: Non-repayable contributions set case by case; see official page
next_steps: Incorporate a profit-oriented company in Canada with 500 or fewer employees
Put the technical work on a Canadian payroll
Call IRAP (1-877-994-4727) to be assigned an Industrial Technology Advisor

name: SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) tax incentive
provider: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Government of Canada
summary: A federal tax credit for eligible research and development work in Canada. Canadian-controlled private corporations get a refundable credit; other claimants get a non-refundable credit.
amount: 35 percent refundable credit on up to CAD 6 million of eligible spending a year for CCPCs (tax years starting after 15 Dec 2024); 15 percent non-refundable for other corporations and individuals
next_steps: Keep time and cost records of the eligible R&D work in Canada
Claim with the income tax return after the year end
Consider a BC corporation (a CCPC) for the 35 percent refundable rate

name: Grand Challenges Canada, Nexa Lighthouse
summary: Transition to Scale funding for proven climate and health innovations that will expand across eligible countries in Asia and the Pacific. Applicant organisations can be incorporated in any country. Full eligibility is in the funding opportunity document.
amount: About US$250,000 to US$2,000,000 per innovation
next_steps: Read the funding opportunity document and the Appendix B country list
Join the information session on 2 Nov 2026
Submit through the Fluxx portal by 17 Nov 2026, 2:00 pm ET (7:00 pm UTC, 3:00 am AWST on 18 Nov)

name: Perago (SFU VentureLabs)
summary: Deeptech accelerator for BC's science-driven innovators tackling global challenges; applications shown as open. VentureLabs also lists Marketing PowerUp and AccelerateIP (open) and ScaleUp Accelerator (closed). Cost, equity and eligibility not stated on the page.
amount: See the official page

deadline.note: Applications shown as open; see the program page

next_steps: Open the Perago page
Confirm BC eligibility and equity terms
Apply

name: Venture Founder (Innovation UBC)
summary: 16 week program for people with a discovery to commercialize or a startup idea. Spring 2027 applications were open until 11 October, so that intake has closed. Other pathways listed: HATCH Venture Builder, Lab2Market, AccelerateIP. Cost, equity and UBC affiliation rules not stated on the page.
amount: See the official page

deadline.note: Spring 2027 intake closed 11 October; check for the next cohort

next_steps: Check the Venture Founder page for UBC affiliation rules
Watch for the next intake
Ask Innovation UBC about alternatives

name: Launch Academy programs
summary: Vancouver tech hub since 2012: Launch Your Startup (24 mentorship sessions), The Revenue Factory (9 week growth program, also an online course), Apollo for international startups exploring North America, and LaunchPad incubation for Western Canada's earliest stage founders. Fees and equity not stated.
amount: See the official page
next_steps: Pick Apollo if based outside Canada
Email info@launchacademy.ca for fees and intake
Compare with the online Revenue Factory

name: Canada Small Business Financing Program (CSBFP)
provider: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, via participating lenders
summary: Government-backed loans and lines of credit from banks and credit unions for Canadian small businesses with up to C$10 million in annual revenue, in all industries except farming.
amount: Up to C$1.15 million in total: term loans up to C$1 million and lines of credit up to C$150,000
next_steps: Ask your bank or credit union whether it offers a CSBFP loan
Use the Find a lender map on Canada.ca/csbfp
Prepare business financials and revenue under C$10 million

name: BDC Small Business Loan and growth financing
summary: Loans and working capital for Canadian businesses that have generated revenue for at least 12 months, generally with at least C$100,000 in annual revenue.
amount: Small Business Loan up to C$350,000; other products (Pivot to Grow loan up to C$2 million) listed on the page
next_steps: Confirm the business is registered in Canada, has a business bank account and 12+ months of revenue
Compare the loan products on the BDC financing page
Book an advisor call with BDC

name: CanExport SMEs
provider: Trade Commissioner Service, Global Affairs Canada
summary: Cost-shared funding for Canadian SMEs to develop new export markets and international business.
amount: Up to C$50,000 per project, assessed on a rolling competitive basis

deadline.note: Intake ended 31 Aug 2026 at 12:00 ET; future intake dates will be posted on the page

next_steps: Read the Applicant's guide 2026-27 and the Find out if you qualify checklist
Prepare an export plan with target markets and costs
Watch the page for the next intake

name: Regional Tariff Response Initiative (BC)
summary: Federal support for incorporated British Columbia businesses hurt by trade disruption: liquidity, competitiveness, market diversification and resilience. Repayable and non-repayable options.
amount: Repayable contributions of C$200,000 to C$10 million per project, interest free, up to 75% of eligible costs for commercial projects; non-repayable liquidity support also available

deadline.note: PacifiCan page dated 16 Oct 2026 says it is accepting applications; no closing date listed

next_steps: Check eligibility: incorporated for-profit in BC, at least C$1 million annual revenue in one of the last two fiscal years, viable before tariffs
Read the applicant guide for SMEs on the PacifiCan site
Contact PacifiCan to confirm which stream fits

name: Community Futures business loans (rural BC)
provider: Community Futures, funded by PacifiCan and the Province of British Columbia
summary: Business loans for rural BC entrepreneurs who find bank credit hard to get, using lending criteria different from a bank's.
amount: Business loans up to C$150,000

deadline.note: Apply through your local Community Futures office

next_steps: Find your office with the Community Futures office finder (34 rural BC offices)
Confirm your business is in a rural BC area served by an office
Ask the office about current rates and eligibility

name: Mitacs Accelerate
summary: Research internships that pair a Canadian for-profit business with a university supervisor and an intern, with Mitacs matching the partner's contribution.
amount: C$15,000 per 4 or 6 month internship (partner C$7,500 plus Mitacs C$7,500); postdoc model C$20,000

deadline.note: No fixed deadline listed; contact a Mitacs Advisor for current intake dates

next_steps: Find an academic supervisor and intern for a research project
Contact a Mitacs Advisor to submit the proposal
Do not start work before the Award Letter is issued

name: EDC Working Capital Guarantees
summary: Guarantees to your Canadian bank that free up working capital for exporters, including the Trade Expansion Lending Program and the Export Guarantee Program.
amount: Export Guarantee Program guarantees up to C$25 million to your lender; other guarantees: See the official page for the current round

deadline.note: Apply through a participating Canadian lender

next_steps: Check you are a registered Canadian exporter with a bank that offers EDC guarantees
Ask your bank about the Trade Expansion Lending Program
Call EDC on 1-800-229-0575 to confirm fit for a small business

name: Go-To-Market Microgrant (BC)
summary: Non-repayable funding for BC for-profit companies with a product or service in market, to speed up repeatable revenue.
amount: C$10,000 to C$50,000 per company, up to 75% of project costs; 25% cash contribution

deadline.note: Currently closed; the last intake ran 17 to 30 Nov 2025; sign up to the Innovate BC Insider newsletter for future calls

next_steps: Check you are incorporated and headquartered in BC with a product in market
Email Microgrant@innovatebc.ca about the next intake
Keep proof of payment for reimbursement

name: Student Entrepreneur Competition (Enactus Canada)
summary: National competition for full-time students at Canadian post-secondary institutions who run a business they own at least 25% of.
amount: C$10,000 champion, C$4,000 runner-up, C$2,000 third place, plus travel to the national exposition for the top 3

deadline.note: 2026-2027 nominations open in October 2026; closing date not listed. Judging Jan to Feb 2027, live final 27 to 30 April 2027

next_steps: Check you are a full-time student at a Canadian institution and a founder with at least 25% ownership
Email programs@enactus.ca to be notified when nominations open
Read the Program and Competition Requirements page; traction is the heaviest scoring item

name: Starter Company Plus (Ontario)
provider: Government of Ontario, delivered by Small Business Enterprise Centres
summary: Ontario program with advisor support, workshops and a mentor, plus a grant for people starting, expanding or buying a small business.
amount: Free advice, training and mentoring; grant of up to C$5,000, with a cash or in-kind contribution of at least 25% of the grant

deadline.note: Apply through your local Ontario Small Business Enterprise Centre; intake varies by centre

next_steps: Find your local Small Business Enterprise Centre on the Ontario page
Check you are 18 or older, an Ontario resident, a citizen or permanent resident, and not in school full-time
Plan your 25% contribution before applying

name: Lab2Market Launch (Pacific hub, BC and Yukon)
provider: Lab2Market with Mitacs, delivered by UBC
summary: Four-month entrepreneurship program for graduate students, postdocs and recent graduates in British Columbia and the Yukon, partly funded through Mitacs.
amount: C$10,000 in stipends at no cost to participants (the page says $10,000; full-time commitment of 30+ hours a week required)

deadline.note: The page gives no start date or deadline; info sessions are listed without a year

next_steps: Check you are a Master's, PhD, postdoc (within 5 years) or recent graduate (within 2 years) in Canada, or a college student
Line up a faculty supervisor
Complete at least 50 customer discovery interviews

name: FrontFundr
summary: Canadian equity crowdfunding platform; FrontFundr Financial Services Inc. is registered as an exempt market dealer in BC, AB, SK, MB, ON, QC, NB, NS and YT. FEES: due diligence and listing fee from CAD 5,500 payable upfront (not refunded on cancellation) plus a trade fee from 7% in cash and warrants on success. NI 45-110 start-up crowdfunding cap is CAD 1.5 million per 12 months; other exemptions have no limit. Works with companies outside Canada.
amount: NI 45-110 cap CAD 1.5 million in 12 months; no overall limit under other exemptions

deadline.note: Apply any time; campaigns usually run 30 to 90 days

next_steps: Submit the application to receive a detailed fee proposal
Budget the upfront CAD 5,500 plus the success fee, and choose the exemption
File a Report of Exempt Distribution in each province you sell into
